izzyondroid:io.github.swiftstagrime.term.description:
Requires Termux to be installed to execute scripts.
 A secure Android bridge for managing and executing scripts via Termux. This app allows you to automate tasks, manage environment variables, and create home screen shortcuts for your favorite scripts with a focus on security and ease of use.
 Features:
 Integrated Script Editor: Write and modify scripts directly within the app.
 Flexible Execution: Support for background execution or interactive Termux sessions.
 Highly Configurable: Support for any file extension.
 Custom prefix commands and arguments.
 Environment variable management.
 Addition of runtime parameters, either with text, or you own presets
 Can be riced with custom themes
 Customization: Personalize your script shortcuts with custom icons.
 Data Portability: Full support for importing and exporting your script library(now with sripts themself and not just my json DTOs parsing)
 ADB and Remote Execution
 You can now trigger scripts remotely via ADB or Webhook service. To use this feature, ensure you have set an "ADB Code" in the script settings (this is empty by default). Run command: adb shell am start \ -n io.github.swiftstagrime.termuxrunner/io.github.swiftstagrime.termuxrunner.ui.features.adbtrigger.AdbTriggerActivity \ --es io.github.swiftstagrime.termuxrunner.adb_code "YOUR_CODE_HERE"
 YOUR_CODE_HERE is supposed to be the code name of the script, like "test2" for example. Webhook example in settings.
 Security First
 I know that scripts often handle sensitive information—whether it's API keys in environment variables or private logic. * Encrypted Storage: All script data and configurations are stored in an encrypted database using SQLCipher.
 Compatibility
 Minimum SDK: 24 (Android 7.0)
 Target SDK: 36 (Android 16)
 OnePlus doesn't like apps installed from unofficial vendors so it blocks ability of the app to cold start Termux, you may want to try and spoof it using adb: 'adb shell pm install -i "com.android.vending" -r name.apk'.
 Other OEMs: If shortcuts do not appear, please manually check your "Background Start" or "Shortcut" permissions in your system settings, NOTE that some flavour might reject the permission later and not send exception to the app, sadly can't do much here.
 Current Status
 This project is currently in early development.
 Testing: Tested various extensions, and all works as expected
 Documentation: Detailed code description is currently under construction.
 Translation: En and Ru are made by me, everything else is AI. You can always switch in settings or during onboarding
 Stability: While functional, you may encounter edge cases. I recommend keeping backups of vital scripts using the built-in export feature. Also, BasicTextField starts lagging while typing at around 177K characters on Snapdragon 7s gen2, Snapdragon 8 gen3 does not have the same expirence. * Random drill generation with configurable action count, thrust count, and five opt-in shaping rules
* Six palettes to choose from per hand, designed and verified for colour-vision-deficiency accessibility
* Export a generated card as a high-resolution PNG or a true-vector, print-ready PDF, or share it directly to another app
* Works fully offline, with no accounts, no analytics, and no network access required
Fechtkarte is free and open-source software (Apache License 2.0), with no proprietary dependencies. See PRIVACY_POLICY.md in the source repository for the full data-handling disclosure.

fdroid:com.wasimaster.wmkeyboard.name: WM Keyboard
fdroid:com.wasimaster.wmkeyboard.summary: A private, offline keyboard: 955 languages, smart typing, themes, and tools.
fdroid:com.wasimaster.wmkeyboard.description:
WM Keyboard is an Android keyboard that keeps its intelligence on your phone. Prediction, autocorrect, glide typing, transliteration, emoji search and learning are all local computation over files in the app's own storage. There is no analytics SDK, no advertising, no account and no server of ours for the app to phone home to. This edition is built with no Google library on its compile classpath at all.
1,555 LANGUAGES, 3,388 LAYOUTS
Native scripts, InScript variants, romanized entries, CJK and constructed languages, all from one data-driven registry. A fresh install starts in the languages your phone is already set to and suggests more from your system language list.
BENGALI THE WAY YOU ACTUALLY TYPE IT
Avro-compatible phonetic typing, so "ami valo achi" becomes আমি ভালো আছি. The phonetic index is lenient: "asi", "achi" and "achhi" all reach the right word. Probhat is there too, with aspirates on shift, plus conjunct-aware backspace.
TYPING THAT LEARNS, LOCALLY
A trie-lattice beam decoder shared by tapping and glide, n-gram context ranking, autocorrect gated by a likelihood ratio rather than a blunt threshold, and on-device learning of your words, bigrams and trigrams. One tap clears all of it.
A REAL TOOLBOX
Clipboard with history, pinning and search. Snippets and text expansion. Calculator, unit and currency conversion, calendars, translate, dictionary lookup, web search, camera, media controls, an app launcher and more, most of them fully offline.
EMOJI, GIFS AND STICKERS
The Emoji 17.0 catalog with semantic search in 125 languages, per-person skin tones, kaomoji, custom sticker packs, and long-press to send animated emoji.
MAKE IT YOURS
A full theme editor: palettes, fonts, key shapes, textures, decals, particles and photo backgrounds, plus Material You and AMOLED. Resize the keyboard, split it, float it, or run it one-handed. Themes and layouts export and import as files, and an addon repository can serve you more.
VOICE AND AI
Speech recognition with a continuous mode, through Android's own recognizer or entirely on the phone: Whisper on whisper.cpp, and Asr4All, Parakeet and Moonshine on ExecuTorch, each model a download you ask for. Harper checks grammar offline. AI writing tools are optional, with your own API key or your own server. Nothing is enabled behind your back.
PRIVACY
Every network feature is a tool you choose to open, and each one is documented. This edition downloads nothing unasked: automatic language data is off by default, so a language's n-gram pack and emoji dictionary arrive only when you accept the prompt or press the button. One connection is not a tool, and it is worth naming: a script with no font of its own is drawn in Noto, fetched through Android's downloadable-fonts provider — Google Play Services where that is installed, and nothing where it is not. Typing on its own never reaches the network: a weather or currency chip waits for your tap before it fetches anything, and exchange rates come from currency-api and Frankfurter, both free software with open data, unless you pick another source. Every service the keyboard uses can also be pointed at another server, including one you run yourself. The update check asks F-Droid only when you press the button for it. Password and secure fields turn off learning, suggestions and clipboard capture on their own, and incognito mode does the same on demand. Backups are written where you point them, and a passphrase encrypts them.
This is the F-Droid build. It leaves out handwriting, text and QR scanning, the Whistle dictation engine and the on-device AI chat models, because they are built on Google libraries or code without published source, and it carries neither. Offline voice libraries come from outside F-Droid, once you allow it. Its privacy policy is its own: https://wmkeyboard.pages.dev/privacy/policy-fdroid/
The full documentation, including exactly what touches the network and when, is at https://wmkeyboard.pages.dev

fdroid:dev.argus.name: Argus
fdroid:dev.argus.summary: Natural-language automation compiled by an LLM, run by a deterministic engine.
fdroid:dev.argus.description:
Argus is a Tasker-class automation app where a large language model is the compiler, not the executor.
You describe a rule in plain language — "every day at 9 send me the BTC price", "when I leave home turn off Wi-Fi", "if an OTP arrives, copy it to the clipboard". The model compiles your request into a structured, typed rule (trigger, conditions, actions). You review it rendered from the types — never from the model's paraphrase — and approve a byte-stable SHA-256 fingerprint of the executable data. From then on a deterministic engine runs the rule: OS alarms, system receivers, geofences, the notification listener. The model is never in the execution loop, except for actions you explicitly mark as generative.
Why this matters:
* Predictable — the rule that fires at 3 a.m. is exactly the one you approved, byte for byte.
* Auditable — every run is logged locally, without personal content.
* Private by design — no Argus-operated backend or account, no telemetry and no analytics. Rules, logs and encrypted API keys stay on your phone; only the provider or self-hosted bridge you explicitly configure receives compile/generative requests.
The language-model transport is pluggable: run a self-hosted bridge, or connect directly to a provider you choose. A base tier works with no elevated privileges; for system-level actions Argus can use Shizuku.
Note: connecting a proprietary provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) is optional — Argus can instead use a self-hosted bridge together with its on-device deterministic actions.
Argus is free software (GPL-3.0). The interface, rule rendering and the agent all follow your system language (English or Italian).

Huallet is the self-custodial wallet of Chihuahua Chain. Hold, send, stake, swap and vote on HUAHUA and the whole Cosmos ecosystem, with your keys encrypted on your phone.
 Your keys, your phone 
 Create a wallet (12 or 24 words, with verification) or import a recovery phrase or private key
 Secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM, key derived from your password (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000 iterations)
 Optional fingerprint or face unlock: the password is kept by the phone's secure hardware (Android Keystore) and released only after a biometric check
 Screenshots blocked, no cloud backup of wallet data, auto-lock
 The recovery phrase is shown only after your password or biometrics
 Ledger hardware wallets over Bluetooth (Nano X, Stax, Flex) or a USB (OTG) cable, with the Cosmos app: keys never leave the device
 Everything Cosmos 
 Portfolio across chains: available, staked, rewards, unbonding
 Staking: stake, unstake, redelegate, claim rewards
 Swap on HuahuaSwap, Chihuahua's native DEX, and on Osmosis with the best route from the Osmosis router
 IBC transfers, channels verified on-chain before sending
 Governance: proposals, live tally, vote
 Chihuahua, Cosmos Hub, Osmosis, Juno and Celestia built in; add any chain from the Cosmos chain registry
 Pay and get paid 
 Scan an address or payment request QR code (in-app scanner, no Google services)
 Tap to pay over NFC: the receiver's phone shares a payment request, the payer's phone reads it. Only the request goes over NFC, never keys or signatures
 Tap a QR code to show it full screen at full brightness
Every transaction is shown in full before you sign. No analytics, no ads, no trackers.
Network connections:
 Public Cosmos RPC/REST endpoints of your chains
 CoinGecko for fiat prices: on by default, can be turned off in Settings. Only token IDs are sent, never your address
 raw.githubusercontent.com for Cosmos chain registry data (asset lists, the chains you add, IBC channels) and token icons; chains.cosmos.directory for the list of chains you can add
 sqs.osmosis.zone for Osmosis swap quotes and raw.githubusercontent.com for the Osmosis asset list, only on the Osmosis swap tab
The icons of the built-in tokens are bundled in the app.

 Sequences loop, so you can go from ace to two or king, in either direction at any time.
 When needed, you can move a card from the stock to the discard pile.
 Other Features:
 Three Layout Options: Beyond the standard TriPeaks layout, the game offers two more layout options.

firefox-addons:2712706.name: Web Component DevTools
firefox-addons:2712706.summary: Developer tooling for Web Components and Web Component Libraries
firefox-addons:2712706.description:
Developer tooling for Web Components and Web Component Libraries
Web Component DevTools is aimed at all developers working with Web Components. The tooling provided creates a new Chrome Devtools panel, which allows a quick look at the custom elements on the current page, and enables modification of attributes and properties of said components.
Web Component DevTools utilizes the Custom Elements Manifest ( https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-manifest ) to analyze the Web Components.
Features:
Web Component DevTools provides advanced features to the developer, straight from the browser's UI to, for example:
- Listing custom elements on the page, and accessible iframes inside the page
- Filtering custom elements on the list
- Inspecting and modifying the attributes of custom elements
- Inspecting and modifying the properties (even objects and arrays) of custom elements
- Observing dispatched events
- Calling functions of the custom element, and logging the return values
Why?
In the process of developing Web Components, wether it be with a library like Lit, or without any kind of library, there comes situtations in which you might want to have a bit more control over your components than what the regular browser devtools gives you.
You might for example want to:
Toggle the Attributes of the element
Toggle the Properties of the element
Monitor when events get dispatched from the element
Call functions
And when you're working with Web Components, Shadow DOM usually is present, making it fairly difficult to find the path to the element. And even if you got the path, having to write document.querySelector("my-selector-string > element-name").setAttribute("my-attr", "foo") every time you want to modify a value is quite cumbersome.
For this use case the Web Components DevTools were created: To enable the developer to easily modify the attributes, properties and therefore state of their element straight from the devtools window with the click of a button.
Issues:
Any issues you run into while using the DevTools should be submitted to the GitHub Repository ( https://github.com/Matsuuu/web-component-devtools/issues ).

firefox-addons:3019859.name: TruHue - Color Season Shopping Companion
firefox-addons:3019859.summary: See which makeup shades are YAY, OKAY, or NAY for your color season while you shop online.
firefox-addons:3019859.description:
COMMON QUESTIONS
Q: I don't know my color season yet — does this work for me?
A: Yes. Take the free 3-minute quiz at truhue.app/app/quiz and set your result in the popup. The widget then scores every shade against your season.
Q: Which retailers does this work on?
A: Sephora, Ulta, Amazon, Target, Walmart, Macy's, Nordstrom, CVS, Walgreens, and the direct-to-consumer stores from MAC, Fenty, Rare Beauty, Glossier, Charlotte Tilbury, NARS, Tarte, ColourPop, e.l.f., and NYX.
Q: Does this work for foundations?
A: Foundation matching uses a separate skin-tone match flow inside the TruHue mobile app. The widget tells you when a product is a foundation and points you there.
Q: Is my browsing data sent anywhere?
A: No. The extension runs entirely in your browser. Only the shade name and product URL of the page you're actively viewing are sent to TruHue's scoring API. No analytics, no tracking, no browsing history is ever shared.
Q: Why are some shades OKAY at 4/10 and others OKAY at 6/10?
A: Higher grade = closer to your palette. A 6/10 OKAY works on most outfits. A 4/10 OKAY is a stretch — wearable as a statement but not a daily go-to.

firefox-addons:1483457.name: GraphQL DevTools
firefox-addons:1483457.summary: Inspect, replay and mock the GraphQL requests of any website. Playground with schema autocomplete, schema explorer, insights, dark theme. Works on desktop and Android.
firefox-addons:1483457.description:
GraphQL DevTools 2.0 — rewritten from scratch.
Every GraphQL request on the page, readable at a glance: operation name, type, duration, result.
What it does
• Request list with operation name, query/mutation/subscription, timing and highlighted errors. Search and filters.
• Formatted query, variables and headers, with a browsable response tree.
• GraphQL errors shown clearly, even when the server answers 200.
• Handles batched requests, persisted queries (APQ) and subscriptions.
• Playground: replay or edit a request, with autocomplete from the schema.
• Schema explorer with types, fields, arguments and deprecations.
• Insights: slowest, most frequent and most failing operations.
• Mock responses: replace an operation's response to test your frontend without touching the server.
• Saved queries, copy as cURL and HAR export.
• Light and dark theme, English and Italian.
On Android too
Firefox for Android has no DevTools: GraphQL DevTools opens from the extension button with a phone-friendly interface.
Privacy
No data leaves your browser: no usage statistics, no external servers.

apple-itunes:6745016854.description:
S7 Communicator brings powerful communication and collaboration tools to your team's mobile devices. Stay connected, productive, and responsive whether you're in the office, at home, or on the go. Keep your business extension with you anywhere.
***Designed for use with the S7 PBX and cloud platform only.***
Key Features of S7 Communicator for Your Team:
* Collaborate Effectively: video & audio calls, group messaging, and seamless file sharing.
* Enable Remote Work: Use your corporate identity for calls, manage communications via your extension, and access contact history.
* Stay Reliably Connected: Get instant push notifications and experience superior call quality, even on unstable networks, thanks to optimized audio codecs.
* Communicate Securely: Benefit from automatic, state-of-the-art encryption protecting your calls, chats, and data.
